mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Home-country notarization, home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation, then Egyptian Consular Legalization (Egypt is not an Apostille member; Hague Apostille is not accepted)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing for each corporate shareholder and foreign ultimate beneficial owner entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or authorized corporate registry authority in the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Home-country notarization, home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation, then Egyptian Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of all natural-person UBOs, shareholders, directors, and intended managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country notary public or authorized attestation officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Home-country notarization, home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation, then Egyptian Consular Legalization; certified Arabic translation after arrival in Egypt

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, authorized signatories, intermediaries, and foreign service providers against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, CBE/EMLCU domestic prohibitions, and the Egyptian public terrorism list. Enhanced due diligence is required for all politically exposed persons (PEPs), family members, and close associates; no PEP or sanctioned person may be admitted as an incorporator, partner, manager, or UBO without EMLCU approval or an applicable legal exemption. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI TAM Unified Investment Portal (tam.gafi.gov.eg) - GAFI name clearance and pre-incorporation filing service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal company name must be in Arabic script and must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered name or a protected trademark. A transliterated Latin-script or English name may be registered only as a supplementary trade name after the Arabic name has been approved; the Arabic name remains the authoritative legal name for registry, judicial, and governmental purposes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation may be extended for one further 30-day period through the GAFI TAM portal upon payment of the applicable renewal tariff before expiry. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with GAFI within 15 working days from notification; GAFI must issue a reasoned decision within 15 working days. A final GAFI refusal may be appealed to the Egyptian Administrative Court within 60 days from the date of notification of the refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a general Egyptian LLC, GAFI accepts a licensed virtual or serviced office as the registered address provided service-of-process is guaranteed. However, for a cross-border payment gateway classified as ISIC 6619 and subject to Payment Systems Law No. 18 of 2019 and Central Bank of Egypt oversight, a physical office in Egypt with local management, records, and compliance personnel is mandatory; a virtual office is not permissible as the sole registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 0.90 - quantified as a 90% probability of unannounced on-site inspection by the CBE, EMLCU, or GAFI during the first 12 months of operation due to the High_Risk_Special_License designation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018), Articles 1, 4, 8 and 26 on Limited Liability Company formation; Executive Regulations Decree No. 96 of 1982; Central Bank of Egypt Law No. 194 of 2020 and Law No. 18 of 2019 Regulating Payment Services.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Department, One-Stop Shop, Cairo.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Contract (Memorandum of Association) executed before an Egyptian Notary Public, accompanied by GAFI Form No. 1 (Notice of Incorporation).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: LLC: no statutory minimum under Companies Law 159/1981; however, Central Bank of Egypt PSP licensing requires minimum paid-up capital of EGP 10,000,000 (~USD 205,000) fully deposited in the company's escrow account at a licensed Egyptian bank before license approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the undersigned incorporators of [Company], an Egyptian Limited Liability Company, adopt the Company Contract dated [date] pursuant to Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended; FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office be situated at [Cairo address] as the company's sole statutory seat; RESOLVED that the initial member quotas in the Company Contract are accepted and fully subscribed; AND RESOLVED that the Members appoint [name] as Managing Director, [name] as Finance Officer, and [name] as AML Compliance Officer, with full power to file registration documents with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones and to apply for the Central Bank of Egypt's Payment Service Provider License, tax card, commercial registration, and ancillary physical clearances.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – One-Stop Shop e-portal (gafi.gov.eg).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic name search and reservation application, proposing three sequential trade name options in order of preference; upon acceptance, obtain the official Name Availability Certificate to lock the entity's legal name.
required_dossiers: Passport photocopies of each founding member
Signed authorization letters appointing the formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File alternative names if the primary proposal is refused for conflict with an existing registered name or trademark; resubmit within 24 hours for administrative review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice – Notary Public Office, Cairo.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute and notarize the Company Contract (Memorandum of Association), including member quotas, registered office clause, and capital provisions, before a licensed notary; authenticate signatures of all founding members and pay notarization stamp duty.
required_dossiers: Member corporate resolutions and identity documentation
Passports or national IDs of all incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct drafting discrepancies identified by the notary and re-execute the contract; appeal notarial queries with additional corporate authorizations if signature validity is challenged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Department – One-Stop Shop, Cairo.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File GAFI Form No. 1 (Notice of Incorporation) together with the notarized Company Contract, bank capital certificate, registered office lease, and initial board resolutions; pay the statutory registration fee and collect the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate confirming capital deposit in escrow
Registered office lease agreement (at least 1 year term)
First board resolution appointing initial officers
Copies of members' passports and national IDs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to GAFI objection notices within 15 calendar days by rectifying lease authenticity, ownership eligibility, or capital documentation; resubmit the corrected dossier through the One-Stop Shop for expedited re-review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry – Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade, Cairo.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the issued company details with the Commercial Registry to obtain the Commercial Registration Certificate and official extract, which is mandatory for all bank, tax, and licensing procedures.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any discrepancies in company particulars and file an amendment application; follow up on registry queries within 5 working days to avoid cancellation of the registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Fiscal File Creation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic tax registration application, obtain the corporate income tax file number and VAT certificate, and activate the electronic e-invoicing system account required for PSP merchant settlement operations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide supplementary site access or authorization documents if the ETA queries physical presence; escalate through a registered tax facilitator to reactivate stalled file creation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Central Bank of Egypt PSP Licensing (Merchant Acquiring and Clearing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Bank of Egypt – Payments Supervision Department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the substantive payment service provider license application under Law No. 18 of 2019, including corporate governance arrangements, AML/CFT compliance manual, IT security architecture, payment-processing business plan, paid-up capital evidence, and board resolutions; obtain provisional and final license approval.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Commercial Registration
Board resolution appointing the compliance officer
AML/CFT policy and internal control manual
Bank certificate evidencing EGP 10,000,000 paid-up capital
Organizational chart and key personnel due diligence
IT infrastructure and security architecture documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Acknowledge CBE deficiency letters in writing within 30 days, provide the requested governance or compliance evidence, and commission an independent external auditor to validate the remedial plan prior to resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Civil Defense and Environmental Occupancy Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) and Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Undertake the fire-safety site inspection, install approved extinguishing and evacuation systems, and file the Category B environmental registration for the office/digital operations facility; obtain the fire safety certificate and occupancy clearance.
required_dossiers: Office lease contract and building structural plans
EEAA Category B environmental registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Satisfy civil defense correction notices by installing the ordered safety equipment and request a site re-inspection; update the EEAA registration if operational footprint changes from administrative to data-center use.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Central Bank of Egypt – Payments Oversight Division (primary licensing); Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (ancillary ICT and data protection clearance).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Payment Service Provider (PSP) License for Merchant Acquiring and Clearing Services (Law No. 18 of 2019).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Environmental Registration required for low-risk administrative/digital infrastructure occupancy; no industrial manufacturing or pollutant discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Law No. 48 of 1982: wastewater discharge exclusively to municipal sewerage with BOD ≤ 60 mg/L, COD ≤ 100 mg/L, TSS ≤ 40 mg/L; standby generator air emissions within Ministry of Environment Decree No. 1255 of 2003 limits; electronic waste handling and disposal per Law No. 9 of 2009.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the General Administration of Civil Defense confirming compliant fire extinguisher placement, illuminated exit signage, and approved emergency evacuation plan; municipal structural and occupancy load inspection for the leased office; workplace safety clearance for non-hazardous administrative operations with no industrial activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance, 15 Lateef El-Barghary Street, Nasr City, Cairo; unified e-services portal https://www.eta.gov.eg with integrated e-invoice/e-receipt, e-filing, and customs single-window (ASYCUDA World) access.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign equity provider must first secure the CBE payment-gateway licence (National Payment Council Law 18/2019) and GAFI incorporation of EG_LLC under Companies Law 159/1981. Statutory TIN procurement: (1) file the ETA registration application (Unified Tax Law No. 85/2020) within 30 days of commercial registration at the competent ETA office; (2) attach GAFI incorporation certificate, MOA, commercial register extract, notarised power of attorney, and the directors'/shareholders' ID documentation; (3) obtain the Permanent Tax Card (Permanent TIN) unifying income tax, VAT, stamp duty, and e-invoicing identifiers; (4) activate ETA e-invoice/e-receipt digital certificates. VAT registration is compulsory within 60 days once taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000 per annum, and voluntary below the threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - EG_LLC is an Egyptian resident juridical person (incorporated in Egypt, central management in Cairo) taxed on worldwide income at the 22.5% corporate rate (Law 91/2005 as amended; 25% for banks/oil, 40% for exploration). No pass-through is available for an LLC; dividends remitted to non-resident shareholders bear 10% withholding tax. A foreign branch would instead be taxed on a deemed 65% taxable base with an additional 5% remittance tax - not applicable to EG_LLC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists under Egyptian tax law; classification follows the registered civil-law form. Available/notable mechanisms: (i) branch of foreign company may apply the deemed 65%-of-profits taxable-base computation instead of full cost allocation; (ii) ETA discretionary VAT group registration for integrated entities; (iii) mainland LLC has no free-zone 0% regime election; (iv) consolidated/group income tax filing is not permitted, each entity files independently; (v) tax treaty relief (double-taxation treaty network) requires prior ETA authorization for reduced withholding.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, administered under the Unified Tax Law No. 85 of 2020
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover (mandatory); voluntary registration is available below threshold; foreign service providers importing services are subject to 14% reverse-charge VAT irrespective of threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: ETA e-invoicing regime (Ministerial Decision 161/2020 and successive roll-out phases 1-7, 2021-2025): all resident companies must integrate their ERP/billing systems with the ETA e-invoice platform through public REST/SOAP APIs; each zero-rated export or domestic invoice is transmitted in near-real-time and validated before issuance (fiscal clearance). The ETA returns a digitally stamped invoice bearing a unique QR-code fiscal code; non-clearance blocks issuance and exposes the taxpayer to fines. The PSP must implement e-receipt (B2C settlement receipts) in parallel under the e-receipt mandate, and maintain real-time merchant-settlement reporting in the CBE-approved scheme.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export goods (VAT Law 67/2016 Art. 24) and services physically/economically rendered to non-residents qualify for 0% VAT, including cross-border acquiring, clearing, and payment-processing services provided to foreign merchants, provided the merchant of record is a non-resident and the benefit is used outside Egypt. The PSP must evidence the foreign counterparty, issue an ETA-cleared zero-rated e-invoice, and show full foreign-currency receipt via Egyptian banks; services partly rendered to Egyptian merchants are apportioned and standard-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (ECS) processed through ASYCUDA World / the Egyptian Single Administrative Window
Bill of lading or air waybill (or truck manifest) evidencing physical departure from Egypt for goods
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by an Egyptian bank evidencing credit of the export proceeds in convertible currency
Commercial invoice, packing list, and certificate of origin issued to the foreign buyer
Foreign merchant contract / PSP merchant agreement demonstrating non-resident status of the beneficiary
ETA-cleared zero-rated e-invoice carrying the QR fiscal code
CBE-licensed PSP operator approval and AML/CTF (Law 80/2002) compliance records for the transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA can reopen assessments within the five-year limitation (extended in fraud/evasion cases). Incorrect or fraudulent zero-rating gives rise to VAT clawback at 14% plus statutory delay interest, per-return fines (EGP 20,000-100,000) for false e-invoicing, and, under Law 91/2005 Art. 134 / Law 67/2016 penalties, fines of one to three times the tax evaded with imprisonment for wilful documentation falsification; customs authorities may concurrently claw back any export refunds and the CBE may blacklist repeat FX-repatriation violators.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains current-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII and a flexible exchange-rate regime introduced in March 2024, with interbank rates determined by market forces and no parallel official rate. Foreign direct investment under Law 72/2017 is protected by statutory guarantees of profit and capital repatriation. In practice, outbound remittances of dividends and invested capital require presentation of audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, valid commercial registration, and underlying transaction documents to an authorized dealer bank. Capital-account transfers remain subject to documentary scrutiny and, occasionally, foreign-currency liquidity timetables, but are not subject to blanket blocking or prior CBE licensing for non-banking entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated through the Egyptian banking system. Under CBE rules, proceeds are normally required to be received within six months from the date of shipment or within thirty days of the stated collection date, depending on the underlying letter of credit or collection instrument. There is no mandatory conversion percentage under the current flexible regime; exporter may retain proceeds in foreign currency accounts or sell them on the interbank market, provided the receipt is traced through an authorized bank and the exporter can demonstrate settlement of underlying obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium for fully offshore digital EMI providers. Egypt's Payment Systems Law (Law 18/2019) and CBE licensing regulations require any payment service provider (PSP) operating in Egypt or processing EGP-denominated merchant payments to obtain CBE authorization or act strictly through a licensed local PSP. Offshore EMIs cannot directly hold EGP settlement accounts or perform local currency clearing; they may integrate as white-label technical infrastructure providers but must not undertake treasury conversion, settlement, or merchant acquiring without a CBE-approved arrangement with an onshore licensed bank or PSP.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: CBE Anti-Money Laundering Rule No. 10 and standard bank KYC policies require physical presence of at least one authorized signatory and every ultimate beneficial owner owning twenty-five percent or more of the LLC during initial onboarding. Remote or video-based identity verification is generally insufficient as the sole measure for non-resident corporate clients. Original passports, board resolutions, certificate of incorporation, commercial register extracts, and Arabic-translated notarized documents must be couriered or submitted through the Egyptian commercial representation channel. A face-to-face interview is mandatory for the compliance sign-off, with dual attestation by the bank's compliance officer and deputy general manager for high-risk PSP clients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registration of the entity as a cross-border payment gateway (ISIC 6619) triggers automatic high-risk categorization under bank AML policy.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide CBE-approved PSP license or a signed outsourcing agreement with a CBE-licensed bank; transaction-monitoring and sanctions-screening architecture; AML/CFT policies approved by the board; segregated trust-account structure for client funds; independent compliance audit report from an Egyptian CPA firm; entity-level risk assessment prepared under CBE instructions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or shareholders domiciled in jurisdictions perceived as offshore or tax-transparent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified true copies of passports, valid commercial licences for every underlying shareholder, bank references from Tier-1 international banks, source-of-wealth declarations, tax residency certificates, professional adverse-media and politically-exposed-persons reports, and a directorship declaration explaining the operational substance of the Egyptian LLC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High expected settlement volume with sub-merchants that cannot be individually identifiable from the LLC's own treasury framework.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed merchant underwriting file for each sub-merchant including compelete onboarding evidence, trade licence, fee matrix, projected transaction profile, an anti-money-laundering audit trail showing traceable fiat settlement to Egyptian banking channels, and the merchant agreement expressly prohibiting wallet-to-wallet shadow settlement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 to a capital sub-account maintained at an authorized dealer bank in Egypt. The supporting wire instruction must include a clear purpose code equivalent to CBE/Egyptian economic classification for direct investment or equity subscription; the LLC must complete the statutory investment affidavit and submit the board resolution, updated commercial register, and passport copies of all UBOs to the bank. For USD-denominated capital, conversion to EGP is performed at the interbank market rate on value date; foreign capital is credited to a blocked or escrow sub-account pending delivery of the Egyptian General Authority for Investment (GAFI) certificate of data entry and completion of the local corporate registration formalities.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury disbursements are settled via SWIFT MT103/PAYMENT orders for genuine trade or service obligations, documentary letters of credit issued under UCP600 for goods transactions, and clean telegraphic transfers supported by tax registration and customs declarations. USD transactions ultimately clear through the correspondent network in New York via CHIPS/Fedwire; EUR transactions clear via TARGET2. EGP-denominated payments are cleared on the CBE Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system. Any outbound remittance exceeding CBE/regulatory thresholds must be backed by the underlying contract, an Egyptian tax card, a valid withholding tax receipt, and, for imports, the import registration and customs Bill of Lading or cargo release; settlement to non-related third parties is generally prohibited unless substantiated by a signed commercial agreement and beneficial-owner certification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forward contracts with CBE-licensed banks for bona fide import, export, dividend, and capital-repatriation programs
FX swaps arranged with authorized banks to manage short-term liquidity mismatches between EGP collections and USD or EUR obligations
Cross-currency swaps for long-term cross-border finance and direct investment exposures
Offshore Egyptian-pound non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) used by non-resident financial counterparts for synthetic EGP hedging without onshore settlement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax annual return with transfer-pricing and related-party disclosure (ETA e-filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year-end (April 30 for December 31 year-end); alternative fiscal year only with ETA approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly delay surcharge of 2% on unpaid tax; late-filing fine; criminal liability of managers for willful default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements approved by the partners' assembly and deposited with GAFI/Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop and Commercial Registry Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months of fiscal year-end for LLCs under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Compliance default recorded by GAFI; managers' personal liability; administrative strike-off risk on prolonged omission

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly VAT and withholding tax returns with annual aggregate reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly period returns due by the end of the following calendar month; annual reconciliation by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 2% per month late-payment penalty under VAT Law No. 67 of 2016; late-filing fines and VAT registration suspension for persistent default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Social insurance monthly contribution statement and annual wage declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly contribution due by the 15th of the following month; annual wage declaration in the first calendar quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 2% monthly late-payment surcharge; criminal liability of managers under Social Insurance Law No. 148 of 2019; NOSI enforcement registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry annual renewal (company continuation registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During January of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Renewal surcharge for late payment; cancellation of commercial registration and loss of legal standing after prolonged default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership (UBO) register annual consistency declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: UBO changes notified within 30 days; consistency attested at the January Commercial Registry renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines and sanction orders under the Companies Law as amended; quota transfers may be suspended until the UBO register is updated

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBE payment service provider annual compliance report, audited financials and systems audit certification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), Payment Systems Oversight
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days of fiscal year-end and not less than 90 days before license expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CBE administrative fines; license suspension or revocation; mandatory cessation of payment services

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CFT compliance report and statistical return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Per FIU directives; usually January 31 for prior calendar year activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties under AML Law No. 80 of 2002; regulatory action against the compliance officer; license revocation risk for PSPs

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size exemption for Egyptian LLCs: every LLC must appoint at least one certified auditor under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and hold an audited partners' assembly; CBE-licensed payment service providers must also meet CBE-specific external and internal audit requirements
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), convergent with IFRS, supplemented by CBE circulars for payment service providers; audit must be conducted in Egypt by a licensed certified auditor

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: UBO declaration filed with the Commercial Registry at incorporation; updates due within 30 days of any ownership change; the January Commercial Registry renewal requires attestation that UBO data remains accurate; for LLC quota transfers by foreign shareholders, the transfer becomes effective against third parties only after register amendment and UBO update
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members/Partners with quota transfer history
Register of Managers (directors) and their legal representatives
Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Law No. 8 of 2022)
Minute books of partners' assemblies (ordinary and extraordinary)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $800 – $2,000 per annum (Cairo registered office, GAFI liaison, and tax agent services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,500 – $8,000 per annum (Egyptian certified external auditor for a payment service provider LLC)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SEZ projects under SEZ Law 83/2002 may qualify for a 5-year income tax exemption; Investment Law 72/2017 grants 30% to 50% investment cost deduction in certain sectors; free-zone entities may enjoy tax relief on export profits. No national blanket tax holiday.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 20 (Juridical Persons Income Tax Return) filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority e-Tax filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year; calendar-year taxpayers must file by 30 April

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Identification Number (TIN) of the Egyptian taxpayer
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Egyptian LLC TIN; do not enter foreign shareholder identifiers in this box

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered address, and commercial registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact Egyptian LLC legal name and official address; no foreign branch details in this box

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year covered by the return and legal form
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the annual period and select 'Limited Liability Company'; non-resident owners are not listed here

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity and economic code
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe merchant acquiring, payment gateway, and payment clearing services; use ISIC 6619 / relevant local code

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue, merchant settlement fees, transaction fees, and other operating income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Egyptian-source revenue earned by the Egyptian LLC; foreign-source income may be taxable if the LLC is a resident taxpayer

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating costs, chargebacks, processing fees, and intercompany expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only arm's length related-party charges are deductible; attach transfer pricing evidence if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss, including offset of prior taxable losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses can be carried forward 5 years; non-resident shareholders cannot claim local losses against foreign income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation at 22.5%, tax credits, final tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only Egyptian withholding tax credits backed by bank evidence; treaty credits for foreign WHT are not granted unless recognised under domestic law

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signatory declaration by the authorised representative
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A sitting director or statutory representative of the Egyptian LLC must sign; foreign shareholder signature is not sufficient

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: monthly penalty of 2% of unpaid tax (capped at 15%), late payment interest at 18% per annum, administrative fine up to EGP 20,000, and risk of an ex parte assessment by the Egyptian Tax Authority

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed by Egyptian companies to resident and non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a DTA reduction, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate from its residence jurisdiction and submit an application to the Egyptian Tax Authority before distribution. The ETA must approve treaty relief; otherwise the Egyptian LLC must withhold 10% on the gross dividend.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 20% statutory tax, DTA rates commonly reduced to 10% to 15%. Interest: 20% statutory tax, DTA rates commonly reduced to 10% to 15% for bank and commercial debt interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory when related-party transactions exceed EGP 5 million per fiscal year; Master File mandatory for MNE groups with consolidated global revenue above EGP 500 million; related-party transaction disclosure form required even below the threshold.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not sustain a full standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to the UAE. General anti-abuse rules, tax recharacterisation powers, and investment licence requirements require genuine commercial activity, local decision-making, employees, and expenditure for an Egyptian payment gateway entity to preserve tax benefits and treaty access.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of merchant acquiring revenues, use of inflated intercompany fees, fabrication of chargeback records, or submission of false transfer pricing documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment for 3 to 5 years, fine of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000, payment of the avoided tax plus 2% monthly delayed penalties and 18% annual interest, prohibition on government contracts, and revocation of e-filing credentials
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and statutory representatives who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the company's tax debt; the ETA can levy personal assets, impose travel bans, and refer the case to criminal prosecution

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Treaty Shopping Entity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Egyptian LLC as a conduit with no office, employees, operational decision-making, or actual payment gateway infrastructure solely to access DTA benefits or favourable SEZ provisions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification of the entire fee flow as taxable income in Egypt, 22.5% corporate income tax, 10% dividend withholding tax on deemed distributions, penalties, and interest; cancellation of SEZ/licence incentives and disqualification from future tax benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil, hold directors personally liable for the additional tax, freeze personal bank accounts, and impose custodial sentences for using sham legal structures to evade tax

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Payment Service Provider Licence Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a cross-border payment gateway without the required Central Bank of Egypt licence, clearing merchants without proper KYC/AML controls, or processing prohibited transactions for sanctioned persons
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cancellation of the payment institution licence, fine of EGP 1,000,000 to EGP 5,000,000 or more, criminal prosecution of responsible officers, seizure of processing funds, and blacklisting from the banking payment network
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners can be personally prosecuted, barred from financial services roles, subjected to asset freezes and travel bans, and imprisoned under the Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Law and Central Bank rules
